title: mark_paid has no idempotency: a retried call records the payment twice
body:
## Summary
`markPaidAction` (examples/ledgerbox/app/actions.ts:336) writes a new payment row on every call, keyed `pay_manual_<invoice>_<Date.now()>` (:360), so a retried or doubled call records the same money twice on the act Undo cannot take back.

## Description
mark_paid is GATED and PERMANENT (lib/tool-classes.ts PERMANENT). The action takes `(ref, amountCents)` and nothing that identifies the REQUEST, so it cannot tell a retry from a second payment: a host that re-sends after a lost answer, a double press on the card's confirm, or an agent that repeats a call it did not see answered each record another row. The balance guard (:350) only stops the total passing the balance, so a partial payment doubles silently. The id also collides when two calls land in one millisecond, and the INSERT then throws out of the action instead of answering. Registry: hitl-approval/resume-after-decision - the continuation 'runs the staged action exactly once ... idempotent against double-delivery of the verdict'; delivery-guarantees names the same rule for effects. Fixed looks like: the tool and the card pass a request key (the gate's approval id), the action records it on the payment and answers a repeat of the same key with the first result.

## Flow
- markPaidAction('LB-2026-0014', 1000) -> ok 'Recorded $10.00'
- the same call again (retry / double press) -> ok again; payments: pay_manual_inv_0014_1792180717532 and ..._534, 1000 each
- fix, in build order: add an optional request key to the action; record it (a payments column, or the activity row); a second call with a seen key returns the first answer; thread the key from BooksTools' mark_paid handler and Decide's confirm

## Expected impact
A person who approved one payment sees one; measured as payment rows per approved request (2 today on a double call). Could break: a caller that deliberately records two equal payments must pass two keys.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one approved mark_paid records exactly one payment
Before: probe 2026-10-16 on the seed: two identical markPaidAction calls -> 2 rows of 1000 cents on LB-2026-0014
After: predicted 1 row, the second call answered with the first result
Method: simulation - Before is a probe; the key has to come from lib/manifest.ts, components/lanes/tools/BooksTools.tsx and components/lanes/card/Decide.tsx, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: a test in examples/ledgerbox/test/: markPaidAction twice with one request key -> one payments row and the same message; with two keys -> two rows; seeded red today (2 rows for one key)

title: A second Send dispatches the older letter the person had replaced
body:
## Summary
`sendReminderAction` sends the newest unsent draft (examples/ledgerbox/app/actions.ts:462); older unsent drafts of the same invoice stay unsent, so the next Send dispatches the letter a redraft replaced.

## Description
draft_reminder adds a row per call and never retires the previous unsent one; send picks `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1` and stamps only that row. After draft gentle -> draft firm -> send (firm goes), the gentle draft is still `sent_at IS NULL`, `has_draft_reminder` stays true, and a second send - an agent repeating the chase, or a person pressing Send on the card that still shows a draft - sends the superseded gentle letter as a second dunning. The send re-check landed this round (32ccf40) does not catch it: the old letter's figures still hold. Registry: hitl-approval/resume-after-decision, 'what runs on approval is not what was shown'. Fixed looks like one unsent draft per invoice: either a redraft supersedes the earlier unsent draft, or a send retires every older unsent draft of that invoice in its transaction - a choice that also decides what undoing a draft restores (see the domain-lib card on undoing a sent reminder's draft).

## Flow
- draftReminderAction(LB-2026-0029, gentle); draftReminderAction(LB-2026-0029, firm)
- sendReminderAction -> sends firm (subject 'LB-2026-0029: $25,350.00 outstanding, 70 days past due')
- sendReminderAction again -> ok 'Sent to Kestrel Labs <...>' - the gentle letter, 2 letters sent for one chase
- fix: pick supersede-at-draft or retire-at-send, then pin 'one unsent draft per invoice' with a test

## Expected impact
A client receives one letter per chase the person approved; measured as letters sent after one redraft and two sends (2 today, 1 after). Could break: the card's draft display and the reminder undo, which assume nothing about older drafts today.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a send dispatches only the letter the person last saw
Before: probe 2026-10-16: two drafts, two sends -> both letters sent (rows: firm sent, gentle sent)
After: predicted the second send answers 'Draft a reminder first' and 1 letter is sent
Method: simulation - Before is a probe; the fix deletes or retires stored drafts and changes what reminder undo restores, a policy the round did not pick alone
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/ledgerbox/app/actions.ts:462  "SELECT id, tone, recipient, subject, body FROM reminders WHERE invoice_id = ? AND sent_at IS NULL ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1"
probe: send 1: true LB-2026-0029: $25,350.00 outstanding, 70 days past due | send 2: true Sent to Kestrel Labs <ines.kaur@kestrel-labs.example>.
rows: [{"tone":"gentle","sent":1},{"tone":"gentle","sent":1},{"tone":"firm","sent":1}]
instrument: a test in examples/ledgerbox/test/: draft gentle, draft firm, send, send -> the second send refused and exactly one reminder stamped sent; seeded red today

title: Every activity row says actor 'user', including an agent's writes
body:
## Summary
All eight `logActivity` calls in examples/ledgerbox/app/actions.ts hard-code `actor: "user"` (:168, :259, :313, :363, :423, :482, :511, :550), so the app's own record cannot tell a person's click from an agent's tool call.

## Description
The same server actions serve two callers: the Lanes' card (a person) and BooksTools' handlers (an agent through document.modelContext). The kit's activity row has an `actor` field for exactly this, and the seed uses 'system' for its rows, but every write from this file says 'user'. After an unattended run nothing in the books says which matches, categorizations or payments the agent made - the question an operator asks first when a figure is wrong. matches.actor is also always 'user' (the INSERT at :248). Registry: observability - a privileged act with no record of who did it. Fixed looks like: each action takes an actor ('user' | 'agent') that BooksTools passes as 'agent' and the card as 'user', written to activity.actor and matches.actor.

## Flow
- agent calls categorize / match_bank_line / mark_paid through BooksTools -> the action logs actor 'user'
- SELECT DISTINCT actor FROM activity -> system, user (never agent)
- fix: add the actor parameter to the actions (this file), pass it from components/lanes/tools/BooksTools.tsx and the card

## Expected impact
An operator can read which writes an agent made; measured as agent writes recorded as 'agent' (0 of N today). Could break: tests that assert actor 'user' (none found).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the books record who made each write
Before: probe 2026-10-16: DISTINCT actor over activity after agent-path writes -> [system, user]
After: predicted BooksTools writes logged 'agent', card writes 'user'
Method: simulation - the actor has to be passed from BooksTools.tsx (ledgerbox-model-tools) and the lanes card (ledgerbox-lanes-ui), outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/ledgerbox/app/actions.ts:168  actor: "user",
examples/ledgerbox/app/actions.ts:259  actor: "user",
examples/ledgerbox/app/actions.ts:313  actor: "user",
grep -c 'actor: "user"' examples/ledgerbox/app/actions.ts -> 8
probe: actors: [{"actor":"system"},{"actor":"user"}]
instrument: test/tool-handlers.test.ts harness: drive categorize through BooksTools' handler and assert the newest activity row's actor is 'agent'; seeded red today

title: Seven more package.json files and the README declare Node 22.5 for the same test hook
body:
## Summary
examples/atlas, demo-kit, hirelane, tidycrm, journey, packages/athena-bridge and the root package.json declare `"node": ">=22.5"`, and README.md:45 says 'Node 22.5+', while hirelane, tidycrm and atlas load their tests through the same `module.registerHooks` hook ledgerbox's does.

## Description
This round made ledgerbox's range true (8079fa5: `^22.18.0 || >=24.0.0`, pinned by test/ledgerbox-app-shell.test.ts against a table of what the tests and node:sqlite need). The same table applies to every example app whose `test/register.mjs` calls `registerHooks` (22.15) and whose test script runs `.ts` files with no strip-types flag (22.18), and the kit's `withTx` needs `DatabaseSync#isTransaction` (22.16) and unflagged node:sqlite (22.13) in every app. The root README's requirement row is the human-facing copy of the same claim. Registry: deployment-contract/platform-build-parity - one declared runtime version, and it must be true. Fixed looks like: each package's engines set from the same table (or a root-level test that evaluates every package.json's range against it), and the README row says 22.18+.

## Flow
- grep '"node"' examples/*/package.json package.json packages/*/package.json -> seven say >=22.5
- grep -l registerHooks examples/*/test/register.mjs -> atlas, hirelane, ledgerbox, tidycrm
- fix: copy the ledgerbox range and its test to each package (or one root test over all), and update README.md:45

## Expected impact
A contributor on Node 22.5-22.17 is told by every package that it is supported and then fails to run the tests; measured as packages whose range admits a version that lacks a required API (7 today, 0 after). Could break: nothing at runtime; pnpm with engine-strict would refuse old Nodes, which is the point.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every declared Node range is one the package runs on
Before: 7 package.json ranges and README.md:45 admit Node 22.5
After: predicted 0, each pinned by the range test
Method: simulation - the instrument exists (examples/ledgerbox/test/ledgerbox-app-shell.test.ts); the files are other contexts' and the README is a shared doc
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/atlas/package.json:34  "node": ">=22.5"
examples/demo-kit/package.json:50  "node": ">=22.5"
examples/hirelane/package.json:40  "node": ">=22.5"
examples/tidycrm/package.json:38  "node": ">=22.5"
examples/journey/package.json:27  "node": ">=22.5"
package.json:17  "node": ">=22.5"
packages/athena-bridge/package.json:24  "node": ">=22.5"
README.md:45  | Node 22.5+ and pnpm 11 | ...
grep -l registerHooks examples/*/test/register.mjs -> atlas, hirelane, ledgerbox, tidycrm
instrument: the engines test from examples/ledgerbox/test/ledgerbox-app-shell.test.ts, run over each package.json (seeded red today on all seven)

title: Two invoice API routes serve a Desk that no longer exists; nothing calls them
body:
## Summary
examples/ledgerbox/app/api/invoices/route.ts and app/api/invoices/[id]/route.ts answer GET with the whole book and any invoice's full detail (client contact and email included), for 'the Desk's command palette' and 'the Desk's split view' - a design the app removed; no code in the repository requests either.

## Description
Both comments (route.ts:7, [id]/route.ts:7) name the Desk, and app/page.tsx:9-13 records that the earlier directions and their routes are gone; the Lanes read the books server-side (page.tsx:21) and agents read them through document.modelContext. `git grep api/invoices` outside docs finds only the context map and the registry map. The routes remain an unauthenticated HTTP surface over the books - every client's contact and email from `getInvoiceDetail` - and the [id] route takes only a raw id, unlike every tool, which takes an id or a number (lib/invoice-ref.ts). Fixed looks like: delete both routes (and the context map's api_surface line on its next scan), or, if a consumer is planned, name it and give the [id] route the shared resolver. Escalated because the routes are this context's declared API surface (context-map.json api_surface 'GET/POST /api/invoices, /api/invoices/[id]'): removing a declared capability is the owner's call.

## Flow
- git grep -n 'api/invoices' -- ':!*.md' -> context-map.json and .ai/registry-map.json only; design/pass3-law-brief.md:543,560 mention it returning 500
- curl http://localhost:3001/api/invoices/inv_0002 (not run: the dev server is another session's) -> the invoice, its client row, matches, payments, reminders
- fix: delete app/api/invoices/**, then typecheck, lint, test

## Expected impact
Two fewer files and no unauthenticated read of client contacts; measured as routes with zero consumers (2 today). Could break: an external script that curls the routes (none in the repository).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no HTTP surface without a consumer
Before: 2 routes, 0 consumers (zero-consumer grep in evidence)
After: 0 routes; gates green (not run - not built)
Method: probe - the zero-consumer grep is the figure; the removal waits on the owner because the routes are the context's declared api_surface
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence:
examples/ledgerbox/app/api/invoices/route.ts:7  /** The slim list the Desk's command palette jumps through. */
examples/ledgerbox/app/api/invoices/[id]/route.ts:7  /** One invoice, end to end, for the Desk's split view (`use()` + Suspense on the client). */
examples/ledgerbox/app/page.tsx:9-13  the Strip ... and a direction index at `/v` ... The index and the Strip's routes are gone; the Lanes IS the app.
$ git grep -n 'api/invoices' -- ':!*.md'
.ai/registry-map.json:6638 / :6639 (paths)
context-map.json:2225 api_surface, :2233, :2237, :2238 (paths)

title: Acts are AUTO because they are reversible, and ledgerbox offers no way to reverse them
body:
## Summary
categorize, match_bank_line, unmatch, draft_reminder and export_summary are classified AUTO on `reversible: true` (lib/tool-classes.ts WRITE), and app/actions.ts stores an undo payload for each, but `undoAction` (app/actions.ts:638) has no caller in the app: no tool, no Trail, no button.

## Description
README 'Host manifest': '`reversible && side_effects !== "external"` is the whole classification rule' - an act runs without a gate BECAUSE it can be taken back. In ledgerbox the taking back exists only as `undoAction`, which `git grep undoAction` finds in app/actions.ts and test/ledgerbox-domain-lib.test.ts and nowhere else; the Lanes render no activity list, BooksTools registers no undo tool (README's tool table has none), and the demo-kit template's ActivityLog page was not carried over. A person cannot remove a draft letter or an export an agent wrote, and cannot undo an agent's categorization of 100 invoices except by re-filing each. Either the app offers undo (an `undo(activity_id)` tool, GATED as tidycrm's is in examples/journey/src/apps.ts:67, and a Trail on the page), or the acts with no other inverse are reclassified - which would gate draft_reminder and export_summary. This round made the unmatch reversal safe (b90473c) so the first option can call it.

## Flow
- git grep -n undoAction -> app/actions.ts:638 and test/ledgerbox-domain-lib.test.ts only
- README tool table: no undo tool; components/: no listActivity reader
- owner decides: expose undo (tool + Trail) or reclassify the acts whose only inverse is undo

## Expected impact
The AUTO class means what the README says it means; measured as reversible acts with a reachable reversal (0 of 5 via undo today; match has unmatch, categorize can be re-filed by hand). Could break: the recorded demo beats if acts become gated.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every act the manifest calls reversible can be reversed by its user
Before: 5 acts declared reversible; 0 reachable undo surfaces (zero-consumer grep)
After: unmeasurable until the owner picks a direction
Method: probe - the grep is the figure; the remedy is a product direction (new tool and UI, or a reclassification that changes what an agent may do without asking)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
